decoding emotions from facial expression and incidental processing fluenty, during attitude formation influences attitude certainty which influences resistance to persuasion.
decoding anger or happiness during the attitude formation process results in higher attitude certainty than decoding sadness.
the diagnosticity of incidental processing fluency experienced in the process of emotion decoding influences attitude certainty, and that attitude certainty influences resistance to persuasion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how attitude certainty influences attitude change and the role of incidental processing fluency as an antecedent of attitude certainty.
the role of emotion decoding in the formation of attitude certainty and the resistance to persuasive appeals.
the role of emotions in attitude change.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
emotion decoding and incidental processing fluencys influence on attitude certainty, in turn, affects attitude change.
the link between decoding anger and attitude certainty is mediated by incidental processing fluency.
emotion decoding and incidental processing fluenty influence attitude certainty, which then influences attitude change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diagnosticity of the processing fluency experienced in the process of emotion decoding is a key determinant of both attitude certainty, and resistance to persuasion.
the more fluent the processing of irrelevant stimuli is, the more certain the attitudes are, which leads to less attitude change.
the fluency of processing irrelevant stimuli during attitude formation influences the diagnosticity of the attitude and thus the degree of attitude certainty.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the way we perceive the world, and how we interpret our experiences, influences our attitudes and the certainty with which we hold our attitudes.
the way we form attitudes is not just a matter of how much we like or dislike an attitude object but also how certain we are about our attitudes.
attitude certainty can serve as an important moderator of attitude change.
